doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Balancing his own music with the Brubeck name
summary: He devotes program space to Take Five and Blue Rondo, playing original and South African music otherwise.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Have you had moments trying to balance your own musical vision with that of your father and people’s expectations when they go to hear any group that has the name “Brubeck” in it.

Look sometimes I wish I didn’t have to devote so much program space to “Blue Rondo” and “Take Five.” But I know that’s — in a way it’s too bad because it’s kind of — it’s an understood contract with the audience and it’s silly to deny that expectation. I mean people come to a concert to have a good time you know. And you don’t want to say well that’s wrong. And it’s, you know again it’s benefitted me terrifically to know that with that platform I can play a lot of original music, and my main — well my programming for years has relied on pretty much a formula that has variations within it, is I know I’m going to end with “Take Five” and even if I’ve played Cecil Taylor, which I don’t — but I mean whatever I play if I end with “Take Five” people will be happy. Okay. So that licenses whatever goes before it. So I play a lot of original music and I’m kind of a campaigner or advocate for South African jazz. So I play those tunes. I don’t play — I used to play a lot of standards in South Africa because again the — you know I was

bringing something from my hemisphere, my side of the Atlantic that they loved, they do pretty well but they always want to learn more about that. But then since I left South Africa I hardly do them. I play original music because people don’t need to pay 20 pounds to hear what they could hear in the back of a pub.
